title: The Garret to the Rue Fortunée: Balzac, the Debts, and the Comédie Humaine
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Touraine, the Nurse and the Cloister

stops.name: Tours: the birth on the street later called Nationale
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the civil register and in every chronology; the hour, eleven in the morning, is carried by the French biographical tradition
stops.campa: A son is born at eleven in the morning to Bernard-François Balzac and Anne-Charlotte-Laure Sallambier, in a house on the street Tours will later name the rue Nationale. The father was born Balssa, a peasant's son from Montirat in the Tarn, and remade the name in Paris somewhere in the decade between 1773 and 1783. He is fifty-two. His wife is twenty-one. Their first child, Louis-Daniel, was born the year before and lived about thirty-three days. This one they call Honoré. The particle he will put in front of it later is not in the register.
suggested_refs: The birth register of Tours, 20 May 1799
Bernard-François Balssa's name change in Paris, dated by the sources only to between 1773 and 1783

stops.name: Saint-Cyr-sur-Loire: four years at the nurse's
stops.date_confidence: the placement is attested by the Maison de Balzac chronology, which gives the arrangement and its roughly four-year duration but no month; the date defaults to the month after the birth
stops.campa: Following the custom of families with a little money, the infant is handed to a wet nurse across the Loire at Saint-Cyr. His mother does not send for him. The brother born the year before had lived thirty-three days, and the mother who buried that one keeps this one at a distance from the start; the distance never closes on either side. He stays at the nurse's until he is about four. When he is brought back into the house at Tours he arrives the way a guest arrives, and the household absorbs him without ceremony.
suggested_refs: The Maison de Balzac institutional chronology for the wet-nurse placement at Saint-Cyr-sur-Loire
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional chronology, as cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Vendôme: six years behind the wall
stops.date_confidence: entry attested to June 1807 and departure to April 1813 by the French chronology; the sources disagree on whether he was eight or ten at entry, and the cause of the departure is not medically established
stops.campa: He is entered as a boarder at the Oratorian college of Vendôme and stays nearly six years under a regime of cold rooms, few holidays, and no going home. Masters remember him as awkward, dreamy, and always reading; they punish him with the alcove, where he reads more. In April 1813 the school hands him back to his family in a condition the biographers call collapse and attribute to too many books. Nothing establishes what it was. Vendôme returns transfigured in Louis Lambert, a novel about a boy whose mind burns out inside a school.
suggested_refs: Louis Lambert (1832), Balzac's own transfiguration of the Collège de Vendôme

stops.name: The Marais: the Pension Lepître and the Lycée Charlemagne
stops.date_confidence: the family move to Paris is dated November 1814; corrected: he attended the Lycée Charlemagne 1814-1816, not 1815-1816. The pin is the rue Charlemagne site and stands about 120 metres from the boarding school on the rue de Turenne, which is folded into this stop
stops.campa: The family moves to Paris in November 1814 and places the boy where a professional career is supposed to start: first a boarding school on the rue de Turenne, then courses at the Lycée Charlemagne in the Marais, where one of his fellow pupils is Jules Michelet. Outside the classroom the capital changes hands twice over, Napoleon at Elba and back and gone again inside a year, while the boy is being fitted for a career in the law. What the street teaches him in those months costs nothing and is not examined. He is fifteen. The registers record nothing else about him.
suggested_refs: The Lycée Charlemagne registers for 1814-1816, which also carry Jules Michelet

segments.name: The Clerk, the Garret, and the Pseudonyms

stops.name: Paris: the machinery of debt, in the étude of Guillonnet-Merville
stops.date_confidence: the clerkships are reconstruction rather than document: the legal-historical scholarship places him with the avoué Guillonnet-Merville from November 1816 to March 1818 and with the notary Passez in 1818-1819. The first law examination of 4 January 1819 is attested; corrected: it was a first examination only, and the degree was never completed
stops.campa: Registered for law, he clerks for the avoué Guillonnet-Merville and afterwards for the notary Passez: three years inside the paper machinery of Paris, marriage contracts, guardianships, seizures, inventories drawn up after a death. He learns what a family looks like reduced to a schedule of sums owed, and the novels will run on that apprenticeship more than on anything Vendôme taught him. On 4 January 1819 he passes a first law examination. He never sits another, and no degree is ever conferred on him.
suggested_refs: Scholarship on Balzac juriste and the notarial instruments that recur throughout the Comédie humaine
sources: Legal-historical scholarship on Balzac's clerkships, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: the trial allowance at 9 rue Lesdiguières
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1819 by the French chronology; the tenancy runs to about 1821
stops.campa: He refuses the notary's practice his family has arranged for him and wins from them a trial instead: two years, a small allowance, and permission to fail. The room is an attic at 9 rue Lesdiguières near the Arsenal, cheap enough that the money goes on firewood and candles rather than furniture. He is twenty. He works there on a five-act tragedy in verse about Cromwell, and he will spend the rest of his life retelling the room, one storey under the roof with the city beneath the window. His parents retire to Villeparisis and wait for the two years to run out.
suggested_refs: The rue Lesdiguières garret as Balzac reworked it in La Peau de chagrin and Facino Cane
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

stops.name: Villeparisis: Cromwell read aloud, and the names that are not his
stops.date_confidence: the tragedy is dated 1820 and the family reading is attested without a month; the pseudonymous novels run 1821-1827 and are folded into this stop
stops.campa: He carries Cromwell out to Villeparisis and reads it aloud to the assembled family. The verdict, delivered by a friend of the house consulted as an authority, is that the author should attempt anything at all except literature. Through the 1820s he writes commercial novels at speed, alone and in collaboration, and signs them Lord R'Hoone, which is an anagram of Honoré, and Horace de Saint-Aubin. He is learning the trade in public under names that are not his own. None of these books is ever admitted to the Comédie humaine.
suggested_refs: The Oeuvres de jeunesse published as Horace de Saint-Aubin and Lord R'Hoone, 1821-1827

stops.name: Paris: Madame de Berny
stops.date_confidence: the verified sources give 1822 and Paris, with no month; the date defaults to May because the relationship is dated May 1822 in the French account of Laure de Berny. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate, not an attested address
stops.campa: Laure de Berny is some twenty-two years older than he is, and married. He is twenty-three. She becomes his lover, his lender, and the first reader whose corrections he accepts, taking manuscripts before anyone else sees them and putting her own money into ventures that swallow it. Everything else he attempts in this decade collapses. He will call her the one person who made him. The relation runs fourteen years, from May 1822 to her death in July 1836.
suggested_refs: Laure de Berny's corrections in the surviving early manuscripts
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: the printer's brevet at 17 rue des Marais-Saint-Germain
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the press operated at number 17 from 4 June 1826 to 1828. Corrected: the coordinate has been moved about 420 metres north from a pin that fell south of the street, which was renamed rue Visconti in 1864
stops.campa: On 4 June 1826 he opens a printing works at 17 rue des Marais-Saint-Germain, with a garçonnière on the floor above, and takes in commercial jobs alongside his own. It follows an earlier scheme, cheap one-volume Molière and La Fontaine, which did not sell. He adds a type foundry under the style Laurent, Balzac et Barbier. By 1828 the presses are gone and by April of that year he has borrowed something near fifty thousand francs. He will be paying for these two years for the remaining twenty-two of his life.
stops.quote: The modern god, the only god in whom faith is preserved, money, is here, in all its power, manifested in a single countenance.
stops.quote_source: Honoré de Balzac, Eugénie Grandet, English translation (Project Gutenberg #1715), written seven years after the press failed
suggested_refs: The rue Visconti, formerly rue des Marais-Saint-Germain, number 17
sources: BnF/Gallica and Maison de Balzac documentation, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: the first book signed Balzac, from the rue Cassini
stops.date_confidence: the rue Cassini tenancy begins in 1828 and no month is carried; the two books described belong to 1829, and the date is set at the start of the tenancy rather than at publication
stops.campa: He takes rooms on the rue Cassini near the Observatoire, and from there publishes Le Dernier Chouan ou la Bretagne en 1800, the first book to carry his own name on the title page. In December of the same year comes the Physiologie du mariage, a mock treatise on marriage and adultery that sells on scandal. One is a researched historical novel; the other is an anatomist's report on how the French actually live. He will work in both registers for the next twenty years. Both books come out in 1829, when he is thirty.
suggested_refs: Le Dernier Chouan ou la Bretagne en 1800 (1829), later revised as Les Chouans
Physiologie du mariage (December 1829)
sources: Maison de Balzac bibliography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Fougères: the Chouans in the field
stops.date_confidence: the stay with General de Pommereul is dated September 1828; the Le Croisic and Guérande journey folded into this stop is dated only to 1830 and is carried as reconstruction
stops.campa: He goes into Brittany in September 1828 and stays with General de Pommereul at Fougères, walking the country where the royalist Chouans fought the Republic thirty years earlier and taking down what men who were there still remember. It is the first time he researches a book instead of inventing it. Two summers later he is on the salt-marsh coast at Le Croisic and Guérande with Madame de Berny, out of Paris while the July Revolution runs its course without him.
suggested_refs: The Chouan country around Fougères, and the salt marshes of Guérande later used as the setting of Béatrix
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

stops.name: Saché: the room upstairs at Margonne's
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the coordinate has been moved about 6.7 kilometres west to the commune of Saché in Indre-et-Loire, from a pin that fell in open country near Pont-de-Ruan. The museum documents roughly a dozen stays; the core run is 1829-1838, wider ranges up to 1848 appear in the dossier. The date is set at the start of the documented run
stops.campa: Jean de Margonne keeps a room for him at the Château de Saché in the valley of the Indre, and he comes back to it about a dozen times over twenty years, usually when Paris and its creditors have become impossible. He works here in bursts, sometimes under his doctor Nacquart's orders to rest and not resting: Le Lys dans la vallée, Eugénie Grandet, stretches of Le Père Goriot and Illusions perdues. The valley under the terrace window is the one he puts the lilies in.
suggested_refs: The Musée Balzac at the Château de Saché, and the manuscripts begun in its upstairs room
sources: Musée Balzac (Château de Saché) institutional documentation, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: the death of Bernard-François
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate and is nominal: the death occurred in the former seventh arrondissement, and no address is carried by the sources
stops.campa: Bernard-François Balzac dies in Paris on 19 June 1829, eighty-two years old, five months after his son's first signed novel comes out. The man who left Montirat as Balssa and arrived in Paris as Balzac had built a career out of provisioning and administration, sat as deputy mayor of Tours, and wanted a notary for a son. He does not see the Comédie humaine, which does not yet have a name and will not have one for eleven years. What he leaves behind him is a widow who will outlive her son, and a surname that two generations earlier belonged to nobody.
suggested_refs: Bernard-François Balssa's administrative career and his deputy mayoralty of Tours, 1803-1808
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

segments.name: The Skin, and the Letter from Odessa

stops.name: Paris: La Peau de chagrin, and a letter signed L'Étrangère
stops.date_confidence: the novel is attested to 1831 without a month. The letter of 28 February 1832 is attested and is folded in here because it answers this book; the pin is his rue Cassini address, where he was living, not an attested delivery point. Corrected: he flirted with candidacy in 1831 and the sourcing for the individual constituencies is weak
stops.campa: La Peau de chagrin appears and makes him famous. A young man finds a piece of shagreen that grants any wish and shrinks with every one, spending its owner's life as it spends his desires. In the same season he lets his name go forward for election in the provinces and nothing comes of it. On 28 February 1832 a letter reaches the rue Cassini from Odessa, unsigned except as L'Étrangère, reproaching him for the women in the book. The writer is Ewelina Hańska, a Polish noblewoman married to Wacław Hański, on an estate in Volhynia.
stops.quote: Possessing me thou shalt possess all things. But thy life is mine, for God has so willed it. Wish, and thy wishes shall be fulfilled; but measure thy desires, according to the life that is in thee.
stops.quote_source: The inscription on the talisman, Honoré de Balzac, The Magic Skin (La Peau de Chagrin), English translation (Project Gutenberg #1307); printed in capitals in the source
suggested_refs: The surviving Lettres à l'Étrangère, beginning with the anonymous letter of 28 February 1832

stops.name: Angoulême: Zulma Carraud's republican table
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the Carrauds lived at Angoulême only from after the 1830 revolution to February 1834, so the open-ended 1830s in the dossier is wrong. No individual stay is dated in the verified sources; the date is set inside the corrected window
stops.campa: Zulma Carraud's husband runs the powder mill at Angoulême, and Balzac comes to stay with them repeatedly until the couple leave for the Berry in February 1834. She is a republican and says so to his face; he is drifting toward the Legitimists and says so to hers; the friendship survives entirely on the arguing, and she is one of the few people who tell him the truth about his books. The town itself, the upper city of families with names and the lower city of paper mills, goes into Illusions perdues almost unaltered.
suggested_refs: Balzac's correspondence with Zulma Carraud, one of the frankest bodies of criticism he received
sources: Research dossier, relationships section on Zulma Carraud

stops.name: Aix-les-Bains: after Madame de Castries
stops.date_confidence: the verified sources carry only the year 1832; the month is set to place the journey after the February letter and is not attested. Corrected: Aix-les-Bains was itself Sardinian territory in 1832, Savoy remaining Sardinian until 1860, so the dossier's phrasing that he went from Aix into the Kingdom of Sardinia is wrong. Also corrected: he abandoned the Chinon candidacy in 1832 after an accident, rather than standing that year
stops.campa: He follows Claire de Castries, marquise de Castries, to Aix-les-Bains in Savoy, which is Sardinian ground, and on toward Geneva. He has read an invitation as more than it was. She does not become his lover, and the humiliation is expensive, because he has paid for the journey with money he does not have. That same year he slips and cracks his head, and drops the parliamentary candidacy he had been weighing at Chinon. He never stands for anything again.
suggested_refs: La Duchesse de Langeais (1834), written out of the Castries episode
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: Eugénie Grandet, dedicated to Maria
stops.date_confidence: the novel is attested to 1833 without a month. The Marie du Fresnay material folded in here was tagged tradition in the dossier and is upgraded: there is a documentary anchor, the 1846 will bequeathing Marie-Caroline a Girardon statue, alongside the letter to his sister, the dedication to Maria, and the reconstruction by Roger Pierrot and André Chancerel. The paternity itself remains probable rather than legally documented. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate
stops.campa: Eugénie Grandet outsells everything he has written: a miser in a house at Saumur, a daughter whose inheritance turns into her sentence, a fortune counted in gold coin that nobody is permitted to spend. He dedicates it to Maria. In the autumn of that year he is with Marie du Fresnay, and on 4 June 1834 she bears a daughter, Marie-Caroline, registered as a child of the du Fresnay household. Balzac's will of 1846 leaves that daughter a statue by Girardon.
stops.quote: Financially speaking, Monsieur Grandet was something between a tiger and a boa-constrictor.
stops.quote_source: Honoré de Balzac, Eugénie Grandet, English translation (Project Gutenberg #1715)
suggested_refs: Balzac's will of 1846 and its bequest to Marie-Caroline du Fresnay
Roger Pierrot and André Chancerel on the du Fresnay paternity

stops.name: Neuchâtel: L'Étrangère in person
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: After a year of letters he meets her, at Neuchâtel, on 25 September 1833, with her husband, her daughter, and the household governess present. He is thirty-four, heavy, and badly dressed. She is a Polish noblewoman whose estate in Volhynia runs to the horizon. What the two of them arrange, on the strength of a year of letters and a few days of conversation, is to wait. Wacław Hański is alive, is not old, and will be alive for another eight years. Neither of them proposes any other course, and the waiting turns out to last seventeen.
suggested_refs: The Neuchâtel meeting of 25 September 1833, first face-to-face encounter of the eighteen-year correspondence
sources: Standard Balzac chronology (Graham Robb, Balzac: A Biography)

stops.name: Geneva: the winter of the second meeting
stops.date_confidence: the stay runs December 1833 to February 1834 and is attested. Corrected: the dossier's Geneva entry had absorbed the first meeting, which belongs at Neuchâtel; Geneva's role is the second meeting, when the relationship became physical
stops.campa: They meet again at Geneva in December and stay into February, ten weeks in the same town, and here the correspondence becomes a physical thing. He works while he is there, because he always works. When he leaves, the arrangement stands where it stood at Neuchâtel: she will not seek a divorce, and he will write to Volhynia and wait. He is by this point the most discussed novelist in France, sued and dunned and printed in three countries at once. He has seen her twice.
suggested_refs: The Geneva stay of December 1833 to February 1834

stops.name: Paris: Le Père Goriot, and the trick that joins the books
stops.date_confidence: written and serialized in 1834, published in book form 1835; the December date marks the start of serialization. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate rather than the fictional rue Neuve-Sainte-Geneviève
stops.campa: He writes Le Père Goriot at speed through the autumn and it begins running in December: a boarding house in a poor street, a retired vermicelli maker being eaten alive by two daughters, a law student learning what Paris charges, and an escaped convict lodging under the name Vautrin. Partway through he does the thing that reorganizes everything he has already written and everything left to write. He brings back characters from earlier books. From here the novels stop being separate objects.
stops.quote: The secret of a great success for which you are at a loss to account is a crime that has never been found out, because it was properly executed.
stops.quote_source: Vautrin to Rastignac, Honoré de Balzac, Père Goriot, trans. Ellen Marriage (Project Gutenberg #1237); the familiar aphorism about great fortunes is a later paraphrase of this line
suggested_refs: The recurring-character system, first worked systematically in Le Père Goriot

stops.name: Vienna: the audience with Metternich
stops.date_confidence: carried as reconstruction: the audience is reported by the Maison de Balzac institutional biography and is dated only to 1835, with no month. The pin is the city, not an attested address
stops.campa: He travels to Vienna and is received by Prince Klemens von Metternich, who has managed conservative Europe since Napoleon fell. Balzac has published views on monarchy, order, and religion as instruments that hold a society together, and the audience flatters them without changing anything. He is a novelist among chancelleries. What was said in the room is not recorded anywhere. The visit survives as a line in an institutional chronology and nothing else.
suggested_refs: The Maison de Balzac chronology for 1835, sole carrier of the Metternich audience
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: a week in the Hôtel des Haricots
stops.date_confidence: the detention is dated 1836 without a month. Corrected: in 1836 the National Guard's disciplinary prison stood at the Hôtel de Bessancourt on the quai Saint-Bernard, where it remained from 1800 to 1837; the pin has been moved about 700 metres to that building, the dossier coordinate having matched none of the prison's three successive sites
stops.campa: The National Guard requires service of him and he does not perform it, so the Guard collects him and puts him for about a week in the disciplinary prison the city calls the Hôtel des Haricots, housed since 1800 in the old Hôtel de Bessancourt on the quai Saint-Bernard and moved along the river again the year after he is let out. He works while he is inside; the sentence costs him a week of copy and nothing else. Of every claim outstanding against him in Paris in 1836, this is the one that collects. It is not persecution and he never says that it is.
stops.quote: Why, then, this Paris of yours is a slough. / And an uncommonly queer slough, too. The mud splashes you as you drive through it in your carriage, you are a respectable person; you go afoot and are splashed, you are a scoundrel.
stops.quote_source: Eugène de Rastignac and Vautrin, Honoré de Balzac, Père Goriot, trans. Ellen Marriage (Project Gutenberg #1237)
suggested_refs: The Hôtel des Haricots and its three successive Paris sites, 1792-1864
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: La Chronique de Paris, and the suit against Buloz
stops.date_confidence: the newspaper venture is dated 1835 and its collapse 1836; the lawsuit is dated June 1836 and is carried as reconstruction, resting on legal-historical scholarship rather than on a fetched judgment. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate
stops.campa: He buys into La Chronique de Paris and edits it, pouring borrowed money into a newspaper that folds inside a year and leaves the debt standing. In the same stretch he takes François Buloz of the Revue des deux mondes to court for sending the proofs of Le Lys dans la vallée abroad to be printed without his consent, and he wins. It is among the earliest French judgments to treat an author's control over his own text as a form of property, and he has to be ruined by the press to bring it.
stops.quote: Journalism is an inferno, a bottomless pit of iniquity and treachery and lies; no one can traverse it undefiled, unless, like Dante, he is protected by Virgil's sacred laurel.
stops.quote_source: Fulgence Ridal to Lucien de Rubempré, Honoré de Balzac, Lost Illusions, English translation (Project Gutenberg #13159)
suggested_refs: The Balzac v. Buloz judgment of June 1836, an early landmark in French authors' rights
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier
Legal-historical scholarship on Balzac juriste, per the research dossier

stops.name: Grez-sur-Loing: the death of Laure de Berny
stops.date_confidence: corrected: she died on 27 July 1836 at Grez-sur-Loing, aged fifty-nine, and the pin has been moved about 65 kilometres from a Paris centroid. Corrected also: the relationship ran fourteen years, May 1822 to July 1836, not the nearly two decades the dossier gives
stops.campa: Laure de Berny dies at Grez-sur-Loing on 27 July 1836, fifty-nine years old, in a village on the Loing sixty-five kilometres from Paris. She had been reading his manuscripts for fourteen years, correcting them in her own hand, and had stopped only when she was too ill to hold them. He is not with her at the end. Le Lys dans la vallée has been out for a few months, with a dying woman at the centre of it. He is thirty-seven, at the height of his production, and the reader he had been writing for is dead.
suggested_refs: Le Lys dans la vallée (1836), whose Madame de Mortsauf is read against Laure de Berny
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Milan: a year at La Scala
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of arrival, 19 February 1837, with a stay of over a year. Corrected: the dossier's blanket range 1836-1838 is too loose. The Italian article corroborates no other Italian city for this period, which leaves the Turin, Venice, Genoa and Florence stops of the dossier on thinner ground than their tags implied; they are folded into this campa rather than pinned
stops.campa: He reaches Milan on 19 February 1837 and stays more than a year, at La Scala and in the Salotto Maffei, received as the author of Eugénie Grandet and lodged by people who can afford him. Part of the business is an errand for the Guidoboni-Visconti family, a lawsuit over an inheritance that requires a man in Italy. The chronologies also place him at Turin, Venice, Genoa, and Florence across these years. Only Milan is firmly documented; the rest of the circuit rests on the dossier alone.
suggested_refs: The Salotto Maffei, Milan, and the Guidoboni-Visconti inheritance suit
sources: Research dossier chronology of 1837-1838 Italian travel

segments.name: Les Jardies and the Silver in the Slag

stops.name: Sèvres: the hillside called Les Jardies
stops.date_confidence: corrected: he settles on the Sèvres slope in 1837 and is forced out by creditors in 1840, not 1841, which is consistent with the Passy move of 1840. The coordinate has been moved about 300 metres to the documented site. No month is carried by the sources, and the month here is set to follow the Milan stay rather than attested. The Nohant week with George Sand, dated only to 1838, is folded into this campa
stops.campa: He buys a hillside at Sèvres called Les Jardies and starts building: a narrow house, terraces, a scheme for pineapples raised under glass and sold in Paris at a franc apiece. The ground slips. Walls come down and go up again. He spends on it money that does not exist, and in 1840 the creditors take it away from him. In the same stretch of years he passes a week at Nohant with George Sand, who owns her land outright and pays for it out of what she writes.
suggested_refs: The Maison des Jardies at Sèvres, and the pineapple scheme recorded in his correspondence
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

stops.name: Sardinia: the slag heaps
stops.date_confidence: the journey is dated 1838 without a month; the date is set inside the documented spring travel. The correspondence establishing the scheme is attested; the mine-site coordinate is approximate. Marseille, Toulon and Corsica, on the outward route, are folded into this campa
stops.campa: In 1838 he goes to Sardinia after silver. The proposition is that the slag left by ancient miners still holds metal worth extracting, and he raises the fare by pawning jewelry and borrowing from his mother and a cousin, travelling by Marseille, Toulon, and Corsica. He reaches the workings and inspects the heaps. The arithmetic in his letters is exact from end to end and the venture produces nothing. He comes back to France having spent borrowed money to look at a pile of rock.
suggested_refs: Balzac's 1838 correspondence on the Sardinian slag-recovery calculations and their financing
sources: Correspondence-based reconstruction in the Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: president of the Société des gens de lettres
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the presidency ran 1839-1840, not to 1841. The pin is a nominal Paris coordinate: the society's 1839 meeting address is not established, and its present seat at the Hôtel de Massa is anachronistic, that building having been moved to the rue du Faubourg-Saint-Jacques only in 1928. The Peytel intervention, dated September 1839, is folded into this stop
stops.campa: He is elected president of the Société des gens de lettres and serves through 1839 and 1840, arguing the writers' case against publishers and newspapers that reprint without paying. It is his own case, because he lives on rights and nothing else. In September of 1839 he publishes a long letter in Le Siècle on the trial of Sébastien-Benoît Peytel, a notary he had known, condemned for murder. He argues the evidence in print, at length, for a man he is not defending in court. Peytel goes to the scaffold.
stops.quote_source: Claude Vignon, in Honoré de Balzac, Lost Illusions, English translation (Project Gutenberg #13159); the sentence following reads that the evil may have its use
suggested_refs: Balzac's Lettre sur le procès de Peytel, Le Siècle, September 1839
The Société des gens de lettres, which in 1891 commissioned Auguste Rodin's monument to Balzac and rejected it in 1898
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier
French Wikipedia, 'Société des gens de lettres'

stops.name: Paris: the treatise on modern stimulants
stops.date_confidence: the Traité des excitants modernes is dated 1839 and was published with Brillat-Savarin's Physiologie du goût; no month. The fifty-cups-a-day figure is carried as tradition: no source establishes a stable count, and the causal link to his death is explicitly unproven in the sources that repeat it. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate
stops.campa: He publishes the Traité des excitants modernes, on wine, tobacco, tea, sugar, and coffee, appended to Brillat-Savarin. He describes taking coffee ground fine on an empty stomach, in quantity, when the work will not start, and what happens afterwards in the head of the man who has taken it. Popular biography has settled on fifty cups a day. No source establishes that figure. The habit is documented and the count is not, and whether the coffee had anything to do with the way he died has never been shown either way.
stops.quote: Dès lors, tout s'agite : les idées s'ébranlent comme les bataillons de la grande armée sur le terrain d'une bataille, et la bataille a lieu. Les souvenirs arrivent au pas de charge, enseignes déployées...
stops.quote_source: Honoré de Balzac, Traité des excitants modernes, section III, Du café (1839), French Wikisource, Oeuvres complètes, Michel Lévy edition, tome 20 (1870)
suggested_refs: Traité des excitants modernes, section III, Du café, on French Wikisource

stops.name: Paris: the candidacy withdrawn at the Institut de France
stops.date_confidence: corrected twice. The pin has been moved to the Institut de France on the quai de Conti; the dossier coordinate fell in the fifth arrondissement and its label conflated the Académie with the Théâtre-Français, a different building. And the episode straddles 1839-1840: Joseph-François Michaud died on 30 September 1839, holding fauteuil 29 and not 26, and the seat went in 1840 to Pierre Flourens, in the election Victor Hugo stood in and lost
stops.campa: The historian Joseph-François Michaud dies on 30 September 1839 holding the twenty-ninth chair of the Académie française, and Balzac puts his name forward for it. Then Victor Hugo enters the same contest and Balzac withdraws rather than be beaten in public by him. Hugo stands and loses anyway; the chair goes in 1840 to Pierre Flourens, a physiologist. Balzac is never elected to the Académie, and never puts his name forward for it again. Its forty chairs are occupied by other men for the whole of his working life.
suggested_refs: The 1840 election to fauteuil 29 of the Académie française, won by Pierre Flourens

stops.name: Paris: Vautrin, one performance at the Porte-Saint-Martin
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the ban follows immediately. The reported cause, that Frédérick Lemaître's wig was read as a caricature of Louis-Philippe, is carried by theatre-history accounts and is not independently established
stops.campa: His play Vautrin opens at the Théâtre de la Porte-Saint-Martin on 14 March 1840, with Frédérick Lemaître in the title part, wearing a wig the audience reads as a caricature of Louis-Philippe. The government bans it the following day and the sets are struck after a single performance. He has been trying for a decade to make the theatre pay what the novels will not, because a hit pays on the night and a novel pays in instalments over years he has already spent. Nothing he writes for the stage ever pays. He writes more plays.
suggested_refs: The suppression of Vautrin, 15 March 1840, and the Frédérick Lemaître costume affair
sources: Maison de Balzac institutional biography, per the research dossier

stops.name: Passy: the door on the other street
stops.date_confidence: occupied from 1840 to 1847; no month is carried by the sources, and the month here is set to follow the loss of Les Jardies to creditors and the Vautrin ban earlier that year rather than attested. The dossier's two lenses differ slightly on the coordinate, 48.8551 against 48.8558, a distance of about 80 metres; the museum address figure is used here. The 1841 Furne consortium contract, signed with Hetzel, Paulin, Dubochet and Sanches, is folded into this campa
stops.campa: He takes the top floor of a house at 47 rue Raynouard in Passy, rented in his housekeeper's name, and lives there seven years. The house is built into a slope, so a caller admitted at the rue Raynouard door can be left standing in the front room while the tenant goes out by the rue Berton, one storey below. Creditors come and miss him. The Guard comes and misses him. In 1841 he signs from here the contract for the collective edition, with Hetzel, Paulin, Dubochet and Sanches; Furne's name goes on the title page, and the scattered output acquires one title.
stops.quote: There's that poor M. Vautrin that they made out to be a convict... Such a lively man as he was, and paid fifteen francs a month for his coffee of an evening, paid you very penny on the nail too.
stops.quote_source: Madame Vauquer on her lodger, Honoré de Balzac, Père Goriot, trans. Ellen Marriage (Project Gutenberg #1237)
suggested_refs: The rue Berton exit below 47 rue Raynouard
The 1841 Furne consortium contract for La Comédie humaine
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

stops.name: Saint Petersburg: the voyage out of Dunkirk
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the dossier tagged the 1841 death of Wacław Hański with a Saint Petersburg pin, conflating two events. Hański died in 1841; Balzac did not reach Saint Petersburg until 1843. The visit is attested to 1843 without a month, and the return by Berlin and Dresden is carried as reconstruction
stops.campa: Wacław Hański died in 1841, and Balzac has been trying to reach the widow since. In the summer of 1843 he sails from Dunkirk, a fortnight at sea, and spends two months near her in Saint Petersburg. He is not well; those around him describe an episode they call an accident méningé. He returns overland by Berlin and Dresden and arrives worn out. She still does not marry him: the estate is unsettled and the Tsar has not given his permission. He is back at the rue Raynouard before the year is out.
suggested_refs: The 1843 Dunkirk-to-Saint Petersburg passage and the overland return through Berlin and Dresden
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology of the 1843 journey, per the research dossier

stops.name: Paris: the Furne corrigé
stops.date_confidence: the corrected Furne set is dated to 1845 without a month, and its role as the basis of modern critical editions is established in Balzac textual scholarship rather than in a single fetched document. The Légion d'honneur appointment of 24 April 1845, folded in here, is attested. The pin is the canonical Paris coordinate
stops.campa: The collective edition, contracted in 1841 and carried through by Furne, prints La Comédie humaine as one work in divisions: studies of manners, philosophical studies, analytical studies, some ninety finished titles and a list of fifty more that will never be written. Then he takes his own printed copy of the definitive text and corrects it in ink, everywhere. That marked-up set, the Furne corrigé, is what modern editors set from. On 24 April 1845 he is made Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur.
stops.quote: French society would be the real author; I should only be the secretary.
stops.quote_source: Honoré de Balzac, Author's Introduction to La Comédie Humaine (1842), in The Human Comedy: Introductions and Appendix, ed. George Saintsbury (Project Gutenberg #1968)
suggested_refs: The Furne corrigé, base text of the modern critical editions and of the Maison de Balzac digital edition
sources: Maison de Balzac digital edition documentation
BnF authority data, per the research dossier

stops.name: Rome: travelling with the Saltimbanques
stops.date_confidence: carried as reconstruction: the 1846 Italian and Swiss travel is dated only to the year in the dossier and no month is fixed. The party's nickname is reported in the same source
stops.campa: He travels in 1846 with Madame Hańska, her daughter Anna, and Anna's husband Georges Mniszech, a party that calls itself the Saltimbanques, the tumblers. In Rome he buys: paintings, furniture, objects, on the standing theory that he is furnishing a house and that everything he acquires is undervalued and will prove it later. A good deal of it is not undervalued. He is buying for rooms in a house that is not yet finished, and the crates go on ahead of him to Paris, consigned to an address he does not yet live in.
suggested_refs: The 1846 Saltimbanques journey through Italy and Switzerland
sources: Research dossier, chronology of 1846 Italian and Swiss travel

stops.name: Paris: the house on the rue Fortunée
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the purchase is attested to 28 September 1846, and the coordinate has been moved about 420 metres west to the rue Balzac, eighth arrondissement, from a pin that fell east of it. The Victor-Honoré material is from surviving correspondence and gives no date beyond the year
stops.campa: On 28 September 1846 he buys a house on the rue Fortunée, an old dependency of the folie Beaujon, and begins filling it for a woman who has not yet agreed to come and live in it. Panelling, a gallery, a bathroom, locks. He never pays the full price. He is forty-seven, and the marriage he is furnishing for has not happened and may not. That same year the two of them expect a child and settle on Victor-Honoré for a son. The pregnancy ends without a living child.
suggested_refs: The rue Fortunée house, renamed rue Balzac in 1850
The correspondence naming the projected child Victor-Honoré
sources: Maison de Balzac chronology, per the research dossier

stops.name: Verkhivnia: the petit Louvre
stops.date_confidence: the first stay runs September 1847 to January 1848 and is attested. Corrected: the coordinate has been moved about 32 kilometres southeast to Verkhivnia in Zhytomyr oblast, from a pin that fell northwest of the estate
stops.campa: He arrives in September 1847 at Wierzchownia in Volhynia, the Hański estate, and calls it her petit Louvre: a manor with more rooms than he can use, wheat running out to the edge of sight, and serfs he counts in his letters the way he counts furniture. He stays until January. No rent, no creditor at the door, no printer's boy waiting in the hall, and for the first time in twenty-five years nobody is dunning him. He also cannot get a line printed from here. Paris is eighteen hundred miles west.
suggested_refs: The Hański manor at Verkhivnia, Zhytomyr oblast

stops.name: Paris: the February Revolution
stops.date_confidence: he returns to France shortly before the revolution; the 24 February date is the abdication of Louis-Philippe, not a dated Balzac movement. The pin is a general central-Paris position for the street fighting
stops.campa: He is back in Paris a few days before the barricades. Louis-Philippe abdicates on 24 February, the Second Republic is proclaimed, and the book trade, the theatres, and the newspapers all stop at once. Balzac's entire economy is credit advanced against publication that has not happened yet, and publication has just been suspended by history. He owns a house on the rue Fortunée he cannot pay for and holds contracts nobody can honour. In September he leaves for Ukraine again.
suggested_refs: The February 1848 collapse of the Paris book and theatre markets

stops.name: Verkhivnia: the second stay, and the last finished book
stops.date_confidence: the second stay runs September 1848 to the spring of 1850 and is attested. The Saché health material of 1848, folded in here, comes from the Musée Balzac chronology and carries no month; the same coordinate correction applies as at the first Verkhivnia stop
stops.campa: He returns in September 1848 and does not leave for eighteen months. His heart is failing. At Saché that summer the signs were already there, and here the breathlessness settles in and the sight begins to go. He works when the body permits and finishes the second part of L'Envers de l'histoire contemporaine, the last thing he ever completes for the Comédie humaine. The list of titles announced and unwritten stays exactly where it is. He waits for the imperial permission, and for her answer.
suggested_refs: L'Envers de l'histoire contemporaine, second part, written at Verkhivnia
sources: Musée Balzac (Château de Saché), per the research dossier

stops.name: Berdychiv: the marriage at Saint Barbara's
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On 14 March 1850 they are married in the Roman Catholic church of Saint Barbara at Berdychiv, a small ceremony with her daughter Anna and her son-in-law Georges Mniszech present. It is seventeen and a half years since the letter came from Odessa. He is fifty and cannot walk far without stopping. She has agreed at last, having first arranged the estate so that it would pass to her daughter and not to the Russian state, which was the point on which seventeen years of the correspondence had hung. They start west in April.
suggested_refs: The church of Saint Barbara, Berdychiv, site of the marriage of 14 March 1850
sources: Research dossier, marriage date and location

stops.name: Paris: the locksmith, and the death on the rue Fortunée
stops.date_confidence: the return is attested to 20 May 1850, his fifty-first birthday, and is folded into this stop. Corrected: the death date is 18 August 1850, given flat by the French and English accounts and by the article on the street; the dossier framed 18 and 19 August as an unresolved standoff, but 19 August is a minority reading reflecting the late hour, not a coequal one. The coordinate is corrected as at the purchase stop
stops.campa: They reach the rue Fortunée on 20 May 1850, his fifty-first birthday, and cannot get in. The servant left in charge has gone out of his mind and does not answer, and a locksmith has to open the door of the house Balzac spent four years furnishing. He is carried upstairs. Gangrene sets into the swollen legs and the heart gives out under it. He dies on the night of 18 August 1850. His mother is in the house. Who else stood in the room that night is disputed, and the fullest account of it was written by a man born eight years after the fact.
suggested_refs: Octave Mirbeau, La Mort de Balzac (1907), a late and disputed account built on stories from the painter Jean Gigoux
The legend of the dying Balzac calling for Horace Bianchon, his own fictional physician, which no contemporary eyewitness source confirms
sources: BnF authority record, per the research dossier

stops.name: Père-Lachaise: the oration at the grave
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the funeral and Hugo's oration were on 20 August 1850, published under that heading in Hugo's collected works; the dossier's afterlife lens gave 21 August and contradicted its own chronology. The burial is in Division 48
stops.campa: He is buried in the forty-eighth division of Père-Lachaise on 20 August. Victor Hugo, who had visited him shortly before the end, helps carry the coffin and speaks at the grave: people in black for the death of a man of talent, a nation in mourning for a man of genius. Nearly every writer in Paris stands on the hill. Sixteen years earlier Balzac had ended Le Père Goriot by putting his young hero on this same slope to look down over the city and declare war on it.
stops.quote: Henceforth there is war between us.
stops.quote_source: Rastignac, looking down on Paris from Père-Lachaise, closing line of Honoré de Balzac, Père Goriot, trans. Ellen Marriage (Project Gutenberg #1237), rendering the French A nous deux maintenant
suggested_refs: Victor Hugo, Funérailles de Balzac, 20 August 1850
The Balzac and Hańska tomb, Père-Lachaise, Division 48

segments.name: The Robe, the Cane, and the House

stops.name: Paris: the rue Balzac house pulled down
stops.date_confidence: the demolition is dated 1890 without a month; the street was renamed rue Balzac in 1850. The shared tomb is attested; the date of Ewelina Hańska's own burial there is not carried by the verified sources
stops.campa: The street is renamed rue Balzac in the year he dies. His widow lives on in the house for decades and is laid in the same tomb at Père-Lachaise. In 1890 the Baroness Adèle de Rothschild has the house taken down. Nothing of it survives above ground: the panelling, the gallery, the locks, the rooms he bought paintings in Rome to fill. A plaque on the garden wall of the Hôtel Salomon de Rothschild marks where it stood. It was the one house he ever owned, and he never finished paying for it.
suggested_refs: The commemorative plaque on the garden wall of the Hôtel Salomon de Rothschild, rue Balzac

stops.name: London: the forty volumes
stops.date_confidence: the Marriage and Saintsbury edition ran 1895-1898 and the rival Philadelphia edition 1895-1900; the date marks the start of publication. Croker's 1836 Quarterly Review attack, folded into this campa, is attested to that year
stops.campa: English readers get him late and incomplete. In 1836 John Wilson Croker had ruled in the Quarterly Review that only a handful of the titles were fit for England: Eugénie Grandet, Le Curé de Tours, Le Médecin de campagne, a few early tales. The first substantially complete English Comédie humaine is Ellen Marriage's, forty volumes edited by George Saintsbury and published in London between 1895 and 1898, with five volumes left out as too shocking for the market. A rival complete version comes out of Philadelphia in the same years.
stops.quote: I have done better than the historian, for I am free.
stops.quote_source: Honoré de Balzac, Author's Introduction to La Comédie Humaine, in the Saintsbury edition (Project Gutenberg #1968)
suggested_refs: Ellen Marriage's forty-volume Comédie humaine, ed. George Saintsbury, London 1895-1898
Friedrich Engels to Margaret Harkness, April 1888, calling Balzac a greater master of realism than all the Zolas past, present and to come
sources: Marxists Internet Archive, Engels to Margaret Harkness, April 1888

stops.name: Passy: the last address standing
stops.date_confidence: the city of Paris acquired the house in 1949; no month carried. The cane is inventory BAL 186 in the museum collection, commissioned from the goldsmith Le Cointe in 1834 for 700 francs on credit and still being paid off in April 1835. Delphine de Girardin's tale is attested to 1836
stops.campa: Of all the addresses he occupied in Paris, only the top floor at 47 rue Raynouard survives. The city buys it in 1949 and it becomes the Maison de Balzac: the small writing table, the chair, an 1842 daguerreotype, and the cane he ordered from the goldsmith Le Cointe in 1834 for seven hundred francs on credit, its pommel set with turquoise and cut with the arms of a noble family he was not related to. In 1836, while he was still alive and still paying for it, Delphine de Girardin published a story in which that cane makes its bearer invisible.
suggested_refs: La canne de Balzac, Maison de Balzac inventory BAL 186
Delphine de Girardin, La Canne de M. de Balzac (1836)
sources: Paris Musées collections, 'La canne de Balzac'
